  MEMORANDUM

TO:  Parking and Traffic Commission
FROM:  Public Works Department
SUBJECT:  Block Party Fees

BACKGROUND:
In May 2007, the Parking and Traffic Commission approved a resolution to adopt requirements and
procedures as a policy for the approval to barricade public streets for block parties. As a result of the
resolution, Public Works was able to standardize the requirements in which Block Party’s would be
approved or denied.

One of the roles Public Works plays in the Block Party process is supplying the Block Party Organizer
with a set of barricades and barriers. If the Block Party application is approved, Public Works drops off
the barriers and barricades on the last working day before the event to the Block Party Organizer for them
to setup the closure of the street on the day of the event. Public Works will then pick up the barriers and
barricades on the first working day after the event.

DISCUSSION:
Currently, the City does not charge a fee to process the permit, to use the City’s equipment or to deliver
and pick-up the equipment. The City of Inglewood has about forty-five (45) block parties on an annual
basis. Fourth of July is the largest and most requested events by the community, ranging from 18-20 block
parties for that day. Also, in addition to block parties, the City supplies barricades and barriers for events
approved by the Permits and Licencing Committee and other various requests by the Police and Fire
Departments. The timeframe for Public Works to prepare and provide the barriers and barricades for a
block party event is 72 hours before the event.

When Public Works delivers the supplies for the event, it usually includes four (4) long barricades with
eight (8) sawhorse legs (this may vary based on street size or access points to the closure). On special
request, Type 1A frames are also provided. This amount provides enough supplies for two (2) barricades
to be set up on each end of the street. Currently, Public Works owns 148 long barricades with 296
sawhorse legs. The table below breaks down the equipment cost loaned out for a block party event:

Works delivered to the resident are either not returned or returned damaged. The most common item

To ensure the longevity of the Block party program and that the barriers and barricades will be delivered

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the Parking and Traffic Commission review the current City of Inglewood fee
structure to the surrounding neighboring City’s and provide Public Works with guidance on the following:
  1. Implementing a fee for the block party and usage of barriers and barricades?
  2. If so, What type of fee? (i.e refundable, non-refundable, rental, etc)

The Parking and Traffic Commission should consider the benefits and impacts it will have on the Block
Party Program.

TO:  Parking and Traffic Commission

FOR:  Peter Puglese, PE TE, City Traffic Engineer

SUBJECT:  Request for Establishment of Permit Parking District for 2nd, 3th and 4th Avenue
  (between W. Manchester Boulevard and W. 88th Street)

SUMMARY:
 It is requested that the Parking and Traffic Commission review the information included in this report and
 conduct a public hearing to receive testimony and consider the recommendation of the City Traffic Engineer
 as to a possible creation of a Permit Parking District

DISCUSSION:
The Public Works Department staff received a petition on July 2018 requesting the formation of a residential
permit parking district on 2nd Avenue between W. Manchester Boulevard and 88th Street due to an influx of
vehicles generated from newly established businesses in the area along Manchester Boulevard and a church in
close proximity to the residential neighborhood. After reviewing the area, the recommended permit parking
district is, 2nd, 3rd and 4th Avenue between W. Manchester Boulevard and W. 88th Street to minimize spillage
of the parking problem to adjacent residential streets. The requested permit parking hours are 7 a.m. to 6 p.m.
seven days a week.

Currently, there is on-street parking on both sides of 2nd, 3rd and 4th Avenues except on street sweeping days
and north of the alley on 2nd Avenue we have 4 hr. parking between 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. except Sundays. The
area is designated as low density residential with commercial fronting Manchester Boulevard. The types of
businesses surrounding these streets by Manchester Boulevard include a medical office, car wash, insurance
offices, auto mechanics, dollar tree and daycare in addition to a church on Van Ness Ave.

Staff has conducted a parking demand analysis of the parking stalls to assess the amount of parking being
utilized daily on both sides of the street. The data was collected on Thursday December 13, 2018 during the
hours of 6 a.m. – 8 p.m. (14 hours).

The information residents request and findings were presented in a staff report to the Parking and Traffic
Commission at the Wednesday February 27, 2019 meeting.  At the meeting the Commissioners requested
additional data be collected on two additional days, a weekday and weekend and once completed be brought
back to the Parking and Traffic Commission to further discuss the findings. The data shown in the next page
tables summarize the number of available parking stalls by percent of occupancy in the AM and PM peak
hours and parking availability by block for the two additional dates of data collected on Sunday March 10,
2019 and Friday March 15, 2019 during the hours of 6 a.m. – 8 p.m. (14 hours) as well as the data previously
collected on Thursday December 13, 2018.

  Based on the three days of data collected and field observations, it does appear parking north of the
  alley is being utilized by the patrons during business hours, which is the intended use. However,
  there is no indication that parking south of the alley is impacted since during peak parking hours

  the formation of a permit parking district.

  The Parking and Traffic Commission needs to weigh the benefits and disadvantages of
  implementing a permit parking district. Based on our study the existing parking conditions provide
  parking for the businesses and residents of these streets.

  It is anticipated that the residents of the area will attend the commission meeting to explain the basis
  for the request.

  Members of the Commission are encouraged to visit the site in advance of the meeting.

  We ask the parking and traffic commission provide direction on the creation of permit parking
  district by:

    Approving the request to begin the voting process or
    Denying the request and terminating the petition process.

 Section 3-76. Establishment of a Permit Parking District.

  Upon the receipt of a petition from the residents and/or business persons of a particular neighborhood
requesting the establishment of a Permit Parking District and citing the reasons for such request, the
Public Works Director or designee shall study the request and the site of the request to determine if a
district is warranted and if there are alternative means to resolve any neighborhood parking problems that
instigated the petition. The Director or designee shall further determine the appropriate boundary of any
prospective district. The petition must bear the signatures of adults from a minimum of ten different
households and/or businesses as evidence of a neighborhood desire to establish a district.
  The findings of the study and recommendations of the Director or designee shall be presented to the
Parking and Traffic Commission at a public hearing. Both petitioners and owners of those properties
fronting on the street(s) that may be included within the district shall be duly notified of the public
hearing. After receiving the recommendation of the Public Works Director and the comments of the
public, the Commission shall determine if the establishment of a Permit Parking District is warranted and
what the boundaries of the district should be. If determined to be warranted by the Commission, the
Public Works Director or designee shall mail or otherwise deliver one questionnaire to each readily
known address within the proposed district (properties fronting on any street or portions of streets that
will be subject to permit parking) requesting approval or disapproval of the establishment of the district.
If a minimum of seventy-five percent of the questionnaires returned to the Public Works Director, within
a minimum period of thirty calendar days, support the establishment of the district, an ordinance
establishing the Permit Parking District shall be submitted to the City Council for consideration and
adoption to amend the Municipal Code accordingly.
(Ord. 2297 3-7-78; Ord. 2339 5-22-79; Ord. 88-3 2-9-88; Ord. 90-9 3-20-90; Ord. 99-17 6-1-99; Ord.
02-05 2-5-02; Ord. 07-04 3-6-07)

Section 3-76.1. Amending or Terminating a Permit Parking District.

  (1) The procedures and criteria, by which an existing Permit Parking District can be amended to
increase the area of the district, or amended to increase the hours and/or days when permit parking is
enforced, shall be pursuant to the procedures set forth in Section 3-76 of this Chapter.
  (2) The procedures and criteria, by which an existing Permit Parking District can be amended to
decrease the hours and/or days when permit parking is enforced, or to terminate permit parking within
part or all of the Permit Parking District, shall be as follows:
  (a) Upon the receipt by the Public Works Director of a petition bearing the signatures of adults from
at least ten different households and/or businesses within the existing district requesting such an
amendment or termination, the Director shall submit the petition and request to the Parking and Traffic
Commission to determine if the amendment or termination is warranted and, if so determined, one
questionnaire will be mailed to each address within the district (or portion of the district subject to the
petition request). If a simple majority (fifty percent plus one) of the questionnaires returned to the Public
Works Director, within a minimum period of thirty days, approve of the amendment or termination, an
ordinance shall be submitted to the City Council to amend the Municipal Code accordingly; or
  (b) If the business activity, that initially caused the neighborhood parking impact and thereby
warranted the establishment of the Parking Permit District, has ceased to exist or no longer has the
potential to create any parking impact on the adjoining residential street(s), the Public Works Director
may report to the City Council that the Permit Parking District is no longer warranted and request that the
 City Council amend the Municipal Code to terminate said district. A consideration to terminate a Permit
Parking District for being no longer warranted may also be initiated by the Parking and Traffic
Commission or by the City Council.
(Ord. 07-04 3-6-07)

Section 3-77. Posting Requirements.

  Signs indicating parking limitations of the respective Permit Parking District pursuant to the
provisions of this Chapter shall be posted in accordance with the provisions of this Code relating to the
posting of traffic regulation signs and shall be deemed duly posted when at least two of such signs are
erected on each side of each street within the block in which any violation occurs.
(Ord. 02-05 2-5-02)

Section 3-78. Permit Issuance and Use Procedure.

  (1) Each household or business located within a Permit Parking District may apply for annual
parking permits with the Police Department or other authorized City department responsible for
reviewing such applications as follows:
  (a) Household. Each household may purchase a maximum of four annual parking permits to be used
by any resident or guest. The applicant shall provide their name, address, driver’s license number, proof
of residence within the Permit Parking District, and any other information requested by the Department
reviewing the application. Permits issued to households may be used by any vehicle parked within the
designated Permit Parking District.
  (b) Business. Each business located within a Permit Parking District may purchase annual parking
permits for its employees. The applicant shall provide its business name, address within the Permit
Parking District, and a current business license. The applicant shall also include the employee’s name,
driver’s license number, and current vehicle registration. The applicant shall provide any additional
information requested by the department reviewing the application. A parking permit shall be specifically
assigned to the employee’s vehicle designated in the application and is non-transferable.
  (2) Full Payment of Fees. All applications shall include full payment of the parking permit fee as
established by City Council resolution. Furthermore, no parking permit shall be issued to any person until
that person has paid all outstanding parking citations, including any civil penalties and related fees.
  (3) Use of Permit. A parking permit shall be displayed within each parked vehicle so that it is
clearly visible from outside of the vehicle by hanging it from the vehicle’s rear view mirror. The permit
shall be removed from the rear view mirror prior to driving the vehicle. A permit is valid only for parking
in the specified parking district and it does not guarantee the availability of a parking space. Parking
permits do not exempt the user from compliance with parking regulations including, but not limited to,
vehicle height or weight restrictions; zones that prohibit the stopping, parking, or standing of all vehicles;
street sweeping; restrictions of the parking space to a particular type of vehicle; or the parking of a vehicle
that is involved in the operation of a street vending business.
  (4) Renewal of Permit. A parking permit shall expire at midnight on December 31st of the year for
which it was issued. It shall be the responsibility of the permittee to apply for a renewal of the permit(s)
on or before that date. An application for renewal of a parking permit shall conform to the requirements
of this Section.
   (5) Revocation of Permit. A parking permit holder shall not sell or rent a parking permit to anyone
else. The holder of a business district parking permit may not give or lend the permit to another person for
their use. A parking permit may not be altered or reproduced. Violation of these provisions shall result in
the revocation of the permit and may result in the revocation of all permits for said permittee, and in the
disqualification of the offending permittee from being issued any future parking permits.
  (6) Replacement of Permits. Any permittee seeking replacement for a lost or stolen permit shall be
assessed a replacement permit fee as established by City Council resolution.
(Ord. 14-09 7-22-14)

Section 3-79. Exceptions from Regulations.

  (1) Only the following vehicles shall be exempted from enforcement of the parking regulations for
Permit Parking Districts:
  (a) Any vehicle bearing a duly issued permit conspicuously displayed on or within the vehicle, said
permit being valid in the subject district.
  (b)  Any licensed physician’s vehicle parked in violation hereof while making a professional call.
  (c)  Any vehicle parked in an individual curbside parking space governed by a parking meter.
  (d) Any vehicle parked in an individual curbside parking space that is specifically exempted by a
posted sign, so long as said vehicle is in compliance with all other parking conditions or limitations
specified on the sign.
  (2) In the event a household will be receiving a large number of guests, the permittee may inform
the Parking Enforcement Division of the place, time and date of the event to which the guests will be
coming. When such notification is made not less than twenty-four hours before
the event, the parking limitations may be exempted during the event’s hours.
